reasoning: Only one profiled variant exists (arm64, OpenMPI 4.1 CPU-only OSU 5.8), so it is the choice by default; it is a genuine MPI communication benchmark, not a base image. accelerator=none and gpu_libs empty, so needs_gpu=false (no CUDA-enabled osu_*_D binaries here). The image bundles the Amazon EFA installer stack (openmpi40-aws, libfabric1-aws, rdma-core) and mca_mtl_ofi.so links libfabric, so the build clearly wants the fast fabric — I list efa first but also allow ethernet since plain OpenMPI TCP BTL works and the benchmark still runs (just slower), keeping the job matchable on non-EFA clusters. At 3 nodes a pairwise point-to-point test would leave a node idle, so I picked osu_allreduce, a collective that meaningfully exercises all 3 nodes and scales with rank count. Message range capped at 1MB with 1000 iterations keeps runtime bounded (~minutes, 600s ceiling is generous). Memory is 0-16GB: OSU allocates only a couple of message buffers per rank (max 1MB here) plus MPI library overhead, a few hundred MB per node at most, so it cannot OOM even on the smallest node. Nodes requested exclusively; no cores/ranks specified so the transform derives ranks per node from the matched cluster, and no arch/gpu vendor supplied since those are stamped from the manifest.
